html:
American writer and humourist, born Samuel Clemens in Missouri, best known for The Adventures of Tom Sawyer (1876) and Adventures of Huckleberry Finn (1884). He grew up in Hannibal, a town on the Mississippi River, which became the world of his best books.

He worked as a printer and then as a steamboat pilot. His pen name comes from the boatmen's call for water two fathoms deep. When the Civil War closed the river, he went west to Nevada and gold rush California, where he tried mining and turned to journalism. His tall tale of a jumping frog made him famous in 1865.

Huckleberry Finn tells of a poor white boy and an escaped enslaved man, Jim, rafting down the river. Written in everyday speech, it mocks the racism of the South. Many writers see it as the start of modern American fiction.

He became a world famous lecturer and a sharp critic of imperialism, opposing the US war in the Philippines. He was born and died in years when Halley's Comet appeared.
